newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC seeks more Calif. power market details.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC seeks more Calif. power market details.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Wednesday urged the three major California utilities to supply more information on their plan to set up a power exchange to sell electricity and offset any market domination.

The commission said it agreed with the California Public Utilities Commission that Pacific Gas and Electric Co, Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, and ENOVA Corp's San Diego Gas & Electric Co might have more market power than their analyses suggested.

The FERC asked the utilities to include in filings due March 31, 1997 information on their contracts and divestiture plans, and asked for a detailed plan explaining who would be responsible for monitoring any changes in market domination and steps to offset it.

The three utilities won preliminary approval from the FERC in November for their plan to set up a power exchange and an independent system operator to handle transmission as part of the state's move to break electricity supply monopolies.
The FERC scheduled a technical conference for January 17 to discuss some of its concerns about transmission capacity, and the costs of transmission, transmission losses, and extra services.
